articles.title: Emery’s new team begin to emerge as Aston Villa rebuild on and off the pitch | Jonathan Wilson
articles.dek: Though they were beaten, the game against Arsenal was one to steady the club’s nerves after a summer of upheaval Nothing ever remains the same. Entropy happens. Evolution…
articles.description: Though they were beaten, the game against Arsenal was one to steady the club’s nerves after a summer of upheaval Nothing ever remains the same. Entropy happens. Evolution happens. People grow, people shrink. The world changes and we must change with it. Change happens. The key is to keep ahead of that change, to guide it. The problem for Aston Villa this summer is that it has felt like change has been happening to them, the understandable desire to rejuvenate the squad coinciding with players being lured away by bigger salaries at more established clubs. The danger is of a vicious spiral, of the exodus inspiring further exodus as faith in the project is lost. This, though, was a game to steady Villa nerves after the embarrassment at Brighton last Saturday – even if there had been a sense of pressure mounting uncomfortably before Bukayo Saka put Arsenal ahead. Villa might even have taken a first-half lead had Emí Buendia’s drive not come back off the bar. The champions were the better side, but there wasn’t a huge gulf between them. There was certainly enough here for Villa fans to believe that, even if this is a period of transition, the team they might turn into at the end of that process could be extremely useful. Continue reading...

articles.title: Lionel Messi’s international retirement serves as a reminder: watch him while you still can
articles.dek: The Argentinian’s international career was singular, and his exit is a reminder that all good things come to an end It was among the defining moments of the 2026 World…
articles.description: The Argentinian’s international career was singular, and his exit is a reminder that all good things come to an end It was among the defining moments of the 2026 World Cup: Lionel Messi standing arms akimbo, looking up towards Argentina’s fervent supporters after losing the final . Tears streamed down his face after his team’s embarrassing loss to Spain in what we now know was Messi’s final match wearing that famous Argentina kit. It was not the first time he’d cried at the tournament. There had been tears of joy in Argentina’s opening match, when Messi rolled back the clock to his glory days with a trio of spectacular goals against Algeria. There had been more when his brace against Austria pushed Argentina through to the knockout round as group winners, and even more when his equalizer against Egypt threw la Albiceleste a much-needed lifeline. Later, the world found out that Messi had been struggling all the while with the health struggles of his father , Jorge, a fact that clearly weighed heavily on him as Argentina made a dramatic return to the final in a bid to defend their 2022 title. Continue reading...
